title: Decomposer performance: profile + parallelize splitByQuality + skip TEASAR on huge meshes
description:
Observed: breasts.obj (374218 verts) takes 157s to decompose. voyage_skull_ref.obj (22107 verts) takes ~10s. The cubic voxel grid in TEASAR is the main suspect but hasn't been profiled.

Profile-first workflow:
1. Instrument each stage of SemanticPatchDecomposer.decompose() with System.nanoTime(). Run on skull / hand / breasts. Identify the top two hotspots.
2. Likely #1: MeshSkeletonExtractor.extract at resolution=128 on a huge mesh. Voxel grid is cubic in mesh_extent/resolution. On 374k verts spanning, say, 2 units, grid is 128³ = 2M voxels, and voxelizeScanline walks faces × YZ bounding box. Fix: auto-drop resolution to 64 when V > 100k, OR skip skeleton entirely for very large meshes and fall back to a bounding-box axis-parallel bucketing.
3. Likely #2: four independent mesh walks for vertex curvature, angle defect, mean curvature, and edge dihedrals. Merge into one walk that accumulates all four per-vertex/per-edge quantities in one pass.
4. Parallelize splitByQuality per patch — each patch's quality scoring + k-means split is independent. User's specific observation.
5. Parallelize assignByNearestBranch over V — current O(V × J) nested loop, trivially parallel.

Target post-fix: skull <5s, breasts <60s.

Separate from PATCH-11 so the quality fix is not gated on perf.
definition-of-done: Instrumented timings checked in. Hotspots identified. Top-two fixes applied. Regression timings attached to the ticket comparing before/after on skull, hand, breasts.
testing-plan: (1) Run decomposer on three meshes pre-fix, log stage timings. (2) Apply fixes. (3) Re-run; timings drop by target factor. (4) Patch count + visual result unchanged within tolerance.
